sanskrit_verse: एषामसंभवे कुर्यादिष्टिं वैश्वानरीं द्विजः । हीनकल्पं न कुर्वीत सति द्रव्ये फलप्रदम् ॥
transliteration: eṣām asaṃbhave kuryād iṣṭiṃ vaiśvānarīṃ dvijaḥ | hīnakalpaṃ na kurvīta sati dravye phalapradam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When higher rituals cannot be performed due to incapacity, a dvija shall perform the Vaisvanara Isti; he shall not perform a deficient ritual when adequate resources exist, as it yields no fruit.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from capacity-consciousness alignment
Causation flows from resource integrity and intention purity
Capacity-based responsibility mandates substitution over omission
Restoration logic requires optimal dharma-karma alignment
Consciousness alignment determines the validity of ritual action
executable_legal_axioms: IF ritual performance capacity < required threshold AND substitute ritual available THEN execute substitute ritual
IF resource adequacy = true AND ritual deficiency = true THEN disallow performance
IF dvija intent = dharma-sustaining AND capacity = aligned THEN authorize substituted yajna
IF ritual outcome = non-fructifying THEN enforce non-performance protocol
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating ritual or constitutional duty failures, the Court must assess capacity thresholds and substitute performance options before determining liability. When sufficient resources exist, failure to perform adequately constitutes actionable misalignment, not mere omission.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana establishes that deficient action in presence of full means is a consciousness disorder, not a punishable offense. Anupurvasah shows intent degradation precedes faulty execution. Proportional responsibility lies in restoring capacity, not inflicting penalty. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that only alignment-based correction restores dharma.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Isti performance completion process under guru supervision
Realign resource assessment and ritual design capabilities
Establish dharmic intent restoration through sankalpa purification
Integrate prana-shuddhi protocols to restore ritual execution capacity
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law is declared: Ritual deficiency is dissolved through conscious substitution, not punitive measure. Dharma prevails by alignment, not force. Consciousness is the ultimate judge.
